title: 2014 HMMT November Guts Problem 13
statement: Let \(A B C\) be a triangle with \(A B=A C=\frac{25}{14} B C\). Let \(M\) denote the midpoint of \(\overline{B C}\) and let \(X\) and \(Y\) denote the projections of \(M\) onto \(\overline{A B}\) and \(\overline{A C}\), respectively. If the areas of triangle \(A B C\) and quadrilateral \(A X M Y\) are both positive integers, find the minimum possible sum of these areas.

solutions.text: 1201 By similar triangles, one can show that \([A X M Y]=2 \cdot[A M X]=\left(\frac{24}{25}\right)^{2} \cdot 2[A B M]=\) \(\left(\frac{24}{25}\right)^{2} \cdot[A B C]\). Thus the answer is \(25^{2}+24^{2}=1201\).
